# Specification Quality Checklist: AI Elements Adoption

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-08-21
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Content Quality

- [x] CHK001 No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs) — requirements are behavioral; the donor component source is named only in Assumptions as procurement provenance, not as a how-to
- [x] CHK002 Focused on user value and business needs — each story frames a learner-facing outcome with the "maintain less" goal carried by success criteria
- [x] CHK003 Written for non-technical stakeholders — stories describe journeys (pick a model, approve a tool ask, review tool activity) without code references
- [x] CHK004 All mandatory sections completed — User Scenarios & Testing, Requirements, Success Criteria all filled

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK005 No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain — reasonable defaults documented in Assumptions (donor block choice deferred to planning with a hard no-runtime-coupling rule)
- [x] CHK006 Requirements are testable and unambiguous — FR-001..FR-009 each state observable behavior (filter+keyboard selection, approval states, collapse defaults, degradation)
- [x] CHK007 Success criteria are measurable — net-LOC non-increase (SC-001), zero new packages (SC-002), ≤2-interaction selection (SC-003), gates green (SC-004), visual review (SC-005)
- [x] CHK008 Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details) — reworded SC-002 to reference "dependency manifest" only as a review artifact; criteria describe outcomes
- [x] CHK009 All acceptance scenarios are defined — 4/4/3 scenarios across the three stories plus 5 edge cases
- [x] CHK010 Edge cases are identified — large model lists, dropped connections, duplicate requests, maintenance mode, keyboard/SR users
- [x] CHK011 Scope is clearly bounded — FR-009 and Assumptions explicitly exclude the message render path, conversation container, prompt input, and deferred blocks
- [x] CHK012 Dependencies and assumptions identified — provenance registry, styling baseline, copy-in ownership model, presentation-layer-only boundary

## Feature Readiness

- [x] CHK013 All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria — each FR maps to at least one acceptance scenario or edge case
- [x] CHK014 User scenarios cover primary flows — model switching (every session), tool approval (safety-critical), tool review (transcript clarity)
- [x] CHK015 Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria — maintainability (SC-001/SC-002), usability (SC-003), safety of convergence (SC-004/SC-005)
- [x] CHK016 No implementation details leak into specification — constitutional invariants referenced only as constraints (no regression to highlighting/branching), never as construction instructions

## Notes

- Validation performed 2026-08-21 in a single pass; one revision applied during validation (SC-002 reworded to remove bundle-tooling language).
- The feature intentionally references a community component registry as its _source of truth for scope_ (which surfaces converge); reviewers accepted this as procurement/scope language rather than implementation detail, since the spec's raison d'être is convergence with an external consensus.
- Constitution alignment pre-checked during authoring: existing UI vocabulary requirement (Core Principle III), progressive degradation (III), bundle-growth justification (IV), and the expound/tree invariants (III) are encoded as FR-005/FR-006/FR-007/FR-008.
- Items marked incomplete would require spec updates before `/speckit.clarify` or `/speckit.plan`; none are incomplete.
